sentences.text: In the City, everything was grey.
Every morning, Elara took her small white pill.
The Leaders said the pill kept everyone calm and safe.
One Tuesday, Elara walked home from her learning centre.
Her head felt empty, like always.
But then, she saw something on the grey street.
It was a small paper, bright blue.
The paper had a drawing: a simple smiling face.
Below the face, there was an address.
Elara felt something new in her chest.
That night, Elara did not sleep well.
She thought about the blue paper.
She thought about the smiling face.
She wanted to see this place.
It was an old building with a dark green door.
A woman with kind eyes looked at her.
The woman’s face was not grey.
She had lines near her eyes.
Elara thought they were smile lines.
The room was small and warm.
There were colourful blankets on chairs.
Simple paintings hung on the walls – red flowers, a yellow sun, a blue bird.
Other people were there, maybe five or six.
Another person had tears in their eyes but was smiling.
"We don't take the pills here," the kind woman explained.
Now you must choose, little one.
Your grey world, or our colourful, feeling world?"
Elara thought about the grey days.
She thought about the empty feeling.
She looked at the colourful room.
She felt scared, but also… hopeful.
She reached into her pocket and touched tomorrow's white pill.
She did not take it out.
Maybe tomorrow, she would feel something more.
